name: Mitral valve area
seoTitle: Mitral valve area Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Mitral valve area: work out LVOT area from the LVOT diameter and the mitral valve VTI. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Mitral valve area calculator works out LVOT area from the LVOT diameter, the mitral valve VTI, the mitral valve area and the mitral valve area (MVA). Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Mitral valve area calculator work?
sections.html:
The Mitral valve area calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports LVOT area in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the method); then you type in the LVOT diameter, the mitral valve VTI, the mitral valve area (MVA) and the mitral valve area (MVA) (2).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Mitral valve area calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

LVOT area=(1 ÷ 4) × PI × (LVOT diameter ^ 2)
LVOT VTI=mitral valve area (MVA) × mitral valve VTI ÷ LVOT area
Pressure half-time (PHT)=220 ÷ mitral valve area (MVA)
Deceleration time (DT)=759 ÷ mitral valve area (MVA)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Mitral valve area calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the LVOT diameter, the mitral valve VTI and the mitral valve area — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Mitral valve area calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns LVOT area, derived from the LVOT diameter, the mitral valve VTI and the mitral valve area. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Mitral valve area calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the LVOT diameter, the mitral valve VTI, the mitral valve area and the mitral valve area (MVA), which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter LVOT diameter in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. LVOT diameter opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Mitral valve area calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
